acceptance_criteria.criterion: DataGrid::pagination() lazily creates and returns a GridPagination instance.
generateOutput() calls renderPaginationRow() in the correct footer position (after repeated header, before actions row).
Pagination does not render when hasProvider() is false.
Pagination does not render when getTotalPages() <= 1.
examples/4-pagination.php loads in a browser with no PHP errors.
Pagination controls render correctly with Bootstrap 5 styling.
Clicking page links navigates to the correct page and shows the correct items.
The 'page X of Y (Z total items)' header line shows correct values.
PHPStan level 6 passes on all modified/new files.

summary: Added pagination(): GridPagination to DataGridInterface with GridPagination import.
Added pagination() lazy-init method to DataGrid.
Integrated renderPaginationRow() call into DataGrid::generateOutput() in the correct footer position: after repeated header row, before actions row.
Pagination guard: only renders when $this->pagination !== null && $this->pagination->hasProvider() (renderPaginationRow() also guards against <= 1 pages internally).

comments.note: DataGrid::generateOutput() guards pagination rendering with $this->pagination !== null && $this->pagination->hasProvider(). The hasProvider() check doubles what renderPaginationRow() already checks internally. The outer null guard is still needed to avoid lazy-creating a pagination object just to check emptiness, so both checks are justified.
No observations on structure — pagination integration follows the same lazy-init pattern as actions() and is consistent with the rest of DataGrid.

summary: QA PASS — all 11 acceptance criteria verified. No visible output corruption because renderActionsRow() guards against empty actions. Will be resolved if the hasActions(): bool interface method is added as recommended in WP-003 QA.

summary: Code review PASS. All 11 acceptance criteria verified via code inspection and confirmed by passing QA. PHPStan reports 0 errors on Bootstrap5Renderer.php, GridPagination.php, and examples/4-pagination.php. The implementation is clean and consistent with WP-003 patterns. Four observations recorded: one medium (JS string injection with unescaped URL template in page-jump onclick), one low (grid ID unescaped in JS context), and two debt entries mirroring architecture issues already tracked from WP-003. None are ACs blockers."

comments.note: Bootstrap5Renderer::createBootstrapPageJumpInput() interpolates $urlTemplate directly into a JavaScript single-quoted string literal: `"...window.location.href = '{$urlTemplate}'.replace(...)"`. If the URL template contains a single quote or backslash (possible in certain URL schemes or if getProvider()->getPageURL() returns encoded chars), the JavaScript will be syntactically broken or exploitable. Fix: use json_encode($urlTemplate) to produce a properly JS-escaped quoted string, e.g. `'window.location.href = ' . json_encode($urlTemplate) . '.replace(...)'`.

createBootstrapPageJumpInput() also injects $inputId (derived from the user-provided grid ID) into the JS onclick string without escaping. A grid ID containing a single quote would break the JS. The grid ID should be either restricted to alphanumeric-plus-hyphen or JS-escaped when embedded in script context.

GridPagination::__construct() takes DataGrid (concrete) rather than DataGridInterface, mirroring the same architecture debt identified in GridActions in WP-003. Only getGrid(): DataGrid is called internally; changing the type hint to DataGridInterface and updating getGrid() return type to DataGridInterface would complete the interface-driven pattern. Deferred, non-blocking.

Bootstrap5Renderer::createBootstrapPaginationRow() calls $this->getColspan() which internally calls $this->grid->actions()->hasActions(), triggering lazy-instantiation of GridActions on grids that have no actions configured. Same lazy-init debt as WP-003. Not a blocker; tracked for future hasActions(): bool on DataGridInterface.
